public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the almost two years since GPT-4 was trained there has been no bona fide GPT-4-sized breakthrough, despite more than $50B invested in going beyond GPT-4 and boasts of exponential progress.
conditions: since GPT-4 was trained/shown in August 2022

statement.excerpt: Which means (it suddently connected for me) that it has been almost two years since there’s been a bona fide GPT-4-sized breakthrough, despite the constant boasts of exponential progress, with no real solution to hallucinations, unreliability, poor reasoning or shaky alignment— even though the field has invested more than $50B in efforts to power beyond GPT-4.

from_speaker: despite the constant boasts of exponential progress
the field has invested more than $50B
in efforts to power beyond GPT-4
our_interpretation: The context anchors the interval to August 2022 and ends it on June 4, 2024. August 1 is an inclusive boundary because no day is specified.

The ordinary reading of a GPT-4-sized breakthrough is a broad capability improvement over GPT-4 comparable to GPT-4's improvement over its predecessor. A narrow benchmark gain alone does not establish that.
Long-context and multimodal advances remain relevant counterevidence because Marcus does not explicitly restrict breakthroughs to text benchmarks.

The money clause is a separate factual commitment. I read dollars as US dollars and invested as resources already committed or deployed toward surpassing GPT-4, while keeping financing, expenditure, and future plans distinct.
The source supplies neither a financial source nor an accounting basis. I therefore record unknown rather than inventing one.
The August 2022 reference is a historical anchor, not an antecedent for a conditional forecast. A demonstration date and completion of training need not be identical.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations across leading models establish no broad advance of the stated scale during the interval, and consistent financial records establish more than USD 50 billion invested specifically toward surpassing GPT-4.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes a qualifying broad breakthrough, or a complete financial accounting on the intended basis establishes that the investment threshold was not exceeded.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI described GPT-4o as GPT-4-level and matching GPT-4 Turbo on English text and code, while reporting gains in other languages, vision, and audio. This supports caution about a broad leap but does not establish the absence of one across the field.

evidence.locator: A note from Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai
evidence.explanation: Google announced a million-token context preview and new long-context capabilities. This is material counterevidence to an unrestricted claim of no breakthroughs, but it does not establish equivalence to the broad GPT-4 leap.

Anthropic reported stronger benchmark performance and improved factual accuracy. These advances must be considered, but a company's announcement does not establish that their magnitude matched GPT-4's earlier leap.

evidence.locator: Private Investment Drops (But We See You, GenAI)
evidence.publisher: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
evidence.explanation: The accompanying paragraph reports $25.2 billion of generative-AI private investment in 2023. That annual financing measure neither establishes nor disproves cumulative spending specifically aimed at surpassing GPT-4.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defensible comparison of capability gains against GPT-4's predecessor baseline, together with a traceable, nonduplicative accounting of investment toward surpassing GPT-4 during the stated interval.
